---
title: Masking and reconstruction
description: "Policies that hide inputs, sample reconstruction targets, or select them with application Booleans."
engine: markdown
---

A mask controls which values the model can see and which values it learns to
predict. The [transaction-history tutorial](../learn/add-transaction-history.qmd)
uses `disputed=rf.Boolean(mask=True)`: every retained transaction's label is
hidden and supervised. That simple policy needs no selector.

This later guide introduces optional policies for hiding ordinary inputs or
reconstructing selected parts of a record. These advanced choices are
independent of [exporting embeddings](../learn/reusable-representations.qmd).

## Choose the intended effect

| Goal | Field configuration |
| --- | --- |
| Supervise every retained occurrence, never embedded | `mask=True` |
| Ordinary input | `mask=False` |
| Train-only learned-mask dropout | `mask=0.15` |
| Train-only structural dropout | `mask=rf.Mask(rate=0.15, skip=True)` |
| Reconstruct sampled values | `mask=rf.Mask(rate=0.15, reconstruct=True)` |
| Reconstruct amounts selected by the application | `mask=rf.Mask(query="routing.hide_amount", reconstruct=True)` |
| Remove an input in every stage without a target | `mask=rf.Mask(skip=True, dropout=False)` |

```{typst}
//| label: fig-masking-policies
//| fig-cap: "What each policy does to one field across five retained transactions, by stage. Sampled policies select one position here for illustration."
//| fig-alt: "A grid with one row per policy and columns for train, validate and test, and predict. mask=True hides and reconstructs every position in every stage. mask=0.15 replaces a sampled position with a learned mask during training only. Mask with rate 0.15 and skip drops a sampled position during training only. Mask with rate 0.15 and reconstruct hides and reconstructs a sampled position during training and validation and is off at prediction. Mask with a query selector and reconstruct hides and reconstructs the selected position in every stage. Mask with skip and dropout false removes the field in every stage."
#policies(
  ("Train", "Validate and test", "Predict"),
  (
    (label: [`mask=True`], cells: (repeat("target", 5), repeat("target", 5), repeat("target", 5))),
    (label: [`mask=0.15`], cells: (("input", "input", "masked", "input", "input"), repeat("input", 5), repeat("input", 5))),
    (label: [`rf.Mask(rate=0.15, skip=True)`], cells: (("input", "input", "skipped", "input", "input"), repeat("input", 5), repeat("input", 5))),
    (label: [`rf.Mask(rate=0.15, reconstruct=True)`], cells: (("input", "input", "target", "input", "input"), ("input", "input", "target", "input", "input"), repeat("input", 5))),
    (label: [`rf.Mask(query="routing.hide_amount", reconstruct=True)`], cells: (("input", "target", "input", "input", "input"), ("input", "target", "input", "input", "input"), ("input", "target", "input", "input", "input"))),
    (label: [`rf.Mask(skip=True, dropout=False)`], cells: (repeat("skipped", 5), repeat("skipped", 5), repeat("skipped", 5))),
  ),
)
```

`mask=True` is shorthand for
`rf.Mask(skip=True, dropout=False, reconstruct=True)`. Under a repeated branch,
this selects every retained transaction. It differs from `mask=1.0`, which
hides every input using learned-mask dropout during training and creates no
reconstruction objective.

Without `skip`, a selected value remains a present coordinate represented by a
learned mask. With `skip=True`, its input content is not tensorized or embedded and
its coordinate is absent from encoder attention. Reconstruction targets still
retain their pristine values for the loss.

A mask selects whole values: one Number, Text value, or Set, for example. It
does not select individual tokens inside Text or members inside Set.

## Configure a policy

| Option | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `query` | Boolean selector in the input; omitted means every retained owner occurrence is eligible. |
| `rate` | Fraction of eligible occurrences to sample; omitted means select all eligible occurrences. |
| `skip` | Omit selected input representations instead of using a learned mask. |
| `reconstruct` | Add an objective for selected observed values, or request predictions. |
| `dropout` | Apply only during training; defaults to `not reconstruct`. |

`dropout=True` and `reconstruct=True` cannot be combined. Rates must be between
zero and one. A zero rate removes the policy; a rate of one normalizes to no
rate, making selection deterministic.

The normalized policy determines when selection runs:

| Policy | Train | Validate/test | Predict |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `dropout=True` | Active | Off | Off |
| `dropout=False`, no rate | Active | Active | Active |
| `dropout=False`, fractional rate | Sampled | Sampled with epoch fixed at zero | Off |

Validation and test use different random streams. Sampling depends on seed,
stage, owner address, epoch, and record layout; do not assume that changing
batching preserves exactly the same selections.

## Select within nested data

A selector is an ordinary Boolean value prepared by the application. For an
optional amount-reconstruction objective, attach `routing.hide_amount` to each
transaction. Here it selects only the middle amount to hide and reconstruct;
the ordinary dispute objective still supervises all three transactions:

```yaml
trxns:
  - booked_at: "2026-05-21T10:00:00"
    amount: 32.00
    merchant: Station Cafe
    disputed: false
    routing:
      hide_amount: false
  - booked_at: "2026-05-27T18:15:00"
    amount: 56.20
    merchant: North Market
    disputed: true
    routing:
      hide_amount: true
  - booked_at: "2026-05-28T14:30:00"
    amount: 84.50
    merchant: North Market
    disputed: false
    routing:
      hide_amount: false
```

The leaf's mask query starts from its containing transaction:

```python
import relflow as rf

model = rf.Model.xs(
    trxns=rf.Branch(
        length=32,
        overflow="tail",
        booked_at=rf.DateParts(
            dateparts=["day_of_month", "day_of_week", "hour_of_day"],
        ),
        amount=rf.Number(
            mask=rf.Mask(query="routing.hide_amount", reconstruct=True),
        ),
        merchant=rf.Category,
        disputed=rf.Boolean(mask=True),
    ),
)
```

```{typst}
//| label: fig-masking-selector
//| fig-cap: "One field can be an input at some positions and a reconstruction target at others. The dispute target stays hidden everywhere."
//| fig-alt: "A payment root owns a repeated trxns branch. Inside it, booked_at DateParts and merchant Category are inputs. The amount Number is hidden and reconstructed where routing.hide_amount is true and an ordinary input elsewhere. The disputed Boolean target is hidden and supervised at every transaction."
#tree(node("payment", kind: "root", children: (
  node("trxns", kind: "branch", repeated: true, children: (
    node("booked_at", type: "DateParts"),
    node("amount", type: "Number", width: 175pt, body: [Hidden and reconstructed where `routing.hide_amount` is true; an ordinary input elsewhere.]),
    node("merchant", type: "Category"),
    node("disputed", kind: "target", type: "Boolean", detail: "Every transaction"),
  )),
)))
```

`routing` is not declared as a model field. The selected amount is represented
by a learned mask and reconstructed from the remaining context. The other
amounts remain ordinary inputs and receive no amount-reconstruction loss.
All dispute labels remain hidden and supervised independently of this choice.

For conditional amount prediction, keep every amount field and selector in
the source schema, using `amount: null` where the requested amount is unknown.
Only selected amount positions have `inferred: true`. The directly bound,
unconditional `disputed` field can be omitted from all prediction transactions.

The selector must provide exactly one non-null Boolean per retained owner
record; integers, lists, missing paths, and null selectors are rejected. A
node's value `query` selects its source value; `Mask.query` independently
selects which owner occurrences receive the policy.

Place a policy on the branch when all descendants should share a decision:

```python
trxns = rf.Branch(
    length=32,
    overflow="tail",
    mask=rf.Mask(rate=0.10, skip=True),
    amount=rf.Number,
    booked_at=rf.DateParts(
        dateparts=["day_of_month", "day_of_week", "hour_of_day"],
    ),
    merchant=rf.Category,
)
```

```{typst}
//| label: fig-masking-branch-policy
//| fig-cap: "A branch policy selects whole transactions. A selected transaction's fields are hidden together, along with any nested descendants."
//| fig-alt: "A grid of three transactions by three fields. The middle transaction is selected by the branch policy, so its booked_at, amount, and merchant cells are all skipped. The other two transactions remain visible inputs."
#tokens(
  ("booked_at", "amount", "merchant"),
  (
    (label: [May 21], values: ([Thu 10:00], [32.00], [Station Cafe])),
    (label: [May 27, selected], values: ([Wed 18:15], [56.20], [North Market])),
    (label: [May 28, latest], values: ([Thu 14:30], [84.50], [North Market])),
  ),
  states: (repeat("input", 3), repeat("skipped", 3), repeat("input", 3)),
  highlight: none, frame-first: false, summary: none,
)
```

Each selected transaction hides all three fields and any nested descendants. A
root mask similarly broadcasts through an observation. Reconstructing branch
or root policies create objectives on active descendant leaves, whose
extensions must support reconstruction.

## Derive a selector

For a separate amount-reconstruction task, a processor can derive a selector
from each transaction's application verification flag. Keep this Boolean
derivation outside the model:

```python
import polars as pl

@rf.preprocess
def select_unverified(frame: pl.DataFrame) -> pl.DataFrame:
    return frame.with_columns(
        trxns=pl.col("trxns").list.eval(
            pl.element().struct.with_fields(
                predict_amount=pl.element()
                .struct.field("amount_verified")
                .fill_null(False)
                .not_(),
            )
        )
    )

amount = rf.Number(
    mask=rf.Mask(query="predict_amount", reconstruct=True),
)
```

Include `amount` inside `trxns` and pass `preprocessor=select_unverified` to its
data module. For direct prediction pass `preprocess=select_unverified` to
`model.predict(...)`. Each source transaction retains the amount field and
verification flag; the processor adds a non-null Boolean selector inside that
transaction before mask resolution.

## Combine policies

Pass a tuple or list of `rf.Mask` objects to combine selections:

```python
amount = rf.Number(
    mask=(
        rf.Mask(rate=0.10),
        rf.Mask(query="routing.hide_amount", skip=True, reconstruct=True),
    ),
)
```

```{typst}
//| label: fig-masking-combined
//| fig-cap: "Two policies on one field during training. Where both select a position, the skip wins and the reconstruction objective remains."
//| fig-alt: "Three rows over five transactions. The sampled learned-mask policy masks the second and fifth positions. The selector policy hides and reconstructs the third and fifth positions. The combined row shows a learned mask at the second position and hidden reconstructed targets at the third and fifth."
#policies(
  ("Train",),
  (
    (label: [`rf.Mask(rate=0.10)`], cells: (("input", "masked", "input", "input", "masked"),)),
    (label: [`rf.Mask(query="routing.hide_amount", skip=True, reconstruct=True)`], cells: (("input", "input", "target", "input", "target"),)),
    (label: [Combined], cells: (("input", "masked", "target", "input", "target"),)),
  ),
  legend: false,
)
```

Ancestor and local selections accumulate. A skip wins over a learned mask;
reconstruction selections accumulate independently. A child policy cannot
restore an input hidden by an ancestor. Duplicate policies are normalized
away.

## Targets during training and prediction

Fitting needs observed target values. Explicit nulls can contribute value-state
objectives for selected nullable fields; structurally absent positions do not
invent labels. Use Boolean dispute labels for all retained transactions in
the basic supervised example, rather than nulls standing in for unknown
outcomes. A fractional reconstruction policy trains its decoder but does not
request ordinary prediction output. To request deterministic reconstruction
later, [update the policy](../guides/schema-mutation.qmd).

A directly bound, unconditional target such as `disputed=rf.Boolean(mask=True)`
may be omitted from prediction input. For a repeated target, its containing
branch records must remain to establish output positions. Targets using an
explicit value query or conditional reconstruction selector still need their
source structure and selector to be bindable.

For example, `disputed=rf.Boolean(query="was_disputed", mask=True)` reads an
explicit source column. Prediction must keep `was_disputed` in every source
transaction, with null for an unknown answer; the direct-binding omission
shortcut does not apply to that query.

Conditional predictions retain their structural positions. Finite and automatic
branch lengths both write variable lists of sibling result structs; a finite
cap does not add public padding. Null collections, empty collections, and null
items remain distinct. See
[repeated coordinates](../reference/prediction-output.qmd#repeated-coordinates).
Use each coordinate's `inferred` flag to identify requested outputs. See
[Prediction output](../reference/prediction-output.qmd) for the Arrow contract.

[Pretraining and fine-tuning](../learn/pretraining-and-fine-tuning.qmd) shows how to change
objectives between training stages. The [evidence catalog](../evidence.qmd)
includes sampled reconstruction, nested selectors, branch ablation, and
prefix-only sequence prediction in P051–P054. The
[evidence from incomplete observations](../evidence/representation/incomplete-evidence.html)
and [contextual-consistency evidence](../evidence/anomaly/contextual-consistency.html)
study missing evidence and reconstruction-based anomaly scores, with their
controls and limitations.
